title: Training module: dispensing adherence and the retail fill adherence allowance
content:
**Prescriptions & Renewals training — the adherence allowance when a prescription moves to a retail pharmacy.**

**The rule.** The adherence allowance follows the days' supply dispensed on this prescription in the last 12 calendar months, adding up the days' supply of every dispensing whose date falls inside that window: 330 days or more allows 90 days; at least 270 but under 330 days allows 60 days; under 270 days allows the retail standard of 30 days. The window is the 12 calendar months before the day of the move, and it is read on that day.

**Questions answered.**

*What is added up?* The days' supply of each dispensing of this one prescription whose dispensing date falls within the 12 calendar months before the move — regular fills and every other dispensing basis alike. Authorizations and voided fills are not dispensings and add nothing.

*Where exactly are the lines drawn?*

| Days' supply dispensed in the 12 months | Adherence allowance |
|---|---|
| 330 or more | 90 days |
| 329 | 60 days |
| 270 | 60 days |
| 269 | 30 days |
| none dispensed | 30 days |

*Is 330 itself enough for 90 days?* Yes: "330 days or more" includes 330. And 270 itself falls in the 60-day band.

**Worked case (hypothetical).** In the 12 months before the move the pharmacy dispensed four fills of 90 days of this prescription, but one of them fell 13 months ago. Only three fall inside the window: 270 days in total, so the adherence allowance is 60 days.
